views.view: No new reserve-management bill purchases for a third straight month; only $14.6bn of reinvestments. The Fed cites a lower projected year-end TGA, overnight rates in the upper part of the ample range, and about $400bn of July-August net bill issuance absorbed with only modest repo pressure. Markets expect purchases to restart around mid-November, though that is not a commitment.

Canadian repo pressure (CORRA above the BoC target) is likely to persist because the frictions are structural, not just low settlement balances. In the US, the SOFR-IORB spread has eased from its peaks but stays more volatile than before as reserve-like assets at the Fed have declined.

Fed funds and repo trade near IORB, overnight rates slightly below it. Purchases are not on a preset path: the Desk is watching October bill issuance and repo pressure and will adjust. Standing repo operations are the ceiling, and Perli supports central clearing of them.
The cut in purchases to zero reflects 'persistently loose funding conditions'. Expected zero again for the next period and perhaps about $10bn a month later in 2026.

Expects no purchases at least through mid-October: less leveraged basis trading, near-record money fund assets, shorter fund maturities and more dealer balance-sheet capacity are all keeping repo soft.
No fundamental shift: the pause is temporary. Expects zero until mid-November, then $5-10bn a month of bill purchases.

Record 112,590 contracts traded in the SOFR-fed funds spread in a day as the Street split on bill supply. Citi: short the August basis at -1.5bp, target -4bp (positioned for SOFR to rise against fed funds). Barclays: the market overreacted to the supply forecast. BofA: July bills put upward pressure on SOFR. Wells Fargo: money funds can absorb only a fraction of July issuance, so cash comes out of private repo, firming SOFR.

SOFR fell to the bottom of the band because Fed bill buying and MBS reinvestment into bills cut net bill supply, and eSLR relief moved repo into uncleared bilateral trades that SOFR excludes. Softness should last near term, but repo should firm over time as deficits lift bill supply, Fed purchases end and the clearing mandate arrives.
